title: Logitech G HUB running
label: Logitech G HUB
reason: G HUB can intercept input from non-Logitech devices and is known to add up to 1 second of input lag on the first key press of a session. If your stick or wheel feels sluggish, this is the most common cause.

title: Logitech Gaming Software (legacy LGS) running
label: Logitech Gaming Software (LGS, legacy)
reason: LGS is the older Logitech driver. Running it alongside G HUB or with non-Logitech input devices causes input conflicts and bind loss. If you also have G HUB installed, uninstall LGS entirely.

title: Razer Synapse running
label: Razer Synapse
reason: Synapse hooks every USB HID device, not just Razer ones. It is a frequent cause of joystick remap failure, double-input bugs, and delayed first key press in flight sims.

title: Corsair iCUE running
label: Corsair iCUE
reason: iCUE's input layer can fight with non-Corsair joysticks and wheels, and is a known source of phantom button presses and stuck axes.

title: SteelSeries GG / Engine running
label: SteelSeries GG / Engine
reason: SteelSeries GG enumerates all HID devices and can disrupt third-party joystick/wheel input even when no SteelSeries hardware is in use.

title: ASUS Armoury Crate running
label: ASUS Armoury Crate
reason: Armoury Crate has a well-documented reputation for adding system-wide input lag and interfering with USB enumeration. If your stick is detected intermittently this is the first suspect.

title: MSI Center / Dragon Center running
label: MSI Center / Dragon Center
reason: MSI's RGB and fan-control layer hooks into USB power management. Reports of joysticks losing power and being re-enumerated mid-game trace back to this.

title: Thrustmaster TARGET running
label: Thrustmaster TARGET (T.A.R.G.E.T.)
reason: TARGET creates a virtual joystick that replaces your real one. If you're using a VKB or non-Thrustmaster stick and TARGET is running, the game will see TARGET's virtual device instead of your real stick.

title: VKB DevCfg open during game session
label: VKB DevCfg
reason: Leaving VKB DevCfg open while playing can intercept the HID stream from your VKB stick. Use DevCfg to configure, then CLOSE it before launching the game.

title: DS4Windows running
label: DS4Windows
reason: DS4Windows is needed to use a DualShock 4 / DualSense as a real joystick — but if Steam Input is ALSO enabled, both will inject input and the controller will fight itself. Pick one: DS4Windows OR Steam Input, not both.

title: Xpadder / JoyToKey running
label: Xpadder / JoyToKey
reason: These tools translate joystick movements into keyboard / mouse events. If a game already supports your stick natively, running these on top creates double inputs and phantom keystrokes.

title: Joystick Gremlin / vJoy running
label: Joystick Gremlin / vJoy feeder
reason: Joystick Gremlin and vJoy are power-user remappers that publish a virtual joystick. Make sure the game is reading from the VIRTUAL stick, not your physical one — otherwise you'll get double inputs across both devices.

title: X360CE running
label: X360CE
reason: X360CE makes any input device look like an Xbox 360 pad. If left running globally it will hijack your joystick / wheel in games that expect a native flight-stick. Only run X360CE per-game.

title: NVIDIA GeForce Experience overlay running
label: NVIDIA GeForce Experience overlay
reason: The in-game overlay adds polling overhead that shows up as occasional input stutter on high-rate joysticks (1000 Hz). The driver itself is fine — only the overlay needs disabling.

title: AMD Adrenalin overlay running
label: AMD Adrenalin overlay
reason: Adrenalin's overlay (Alt+R) and instant-replay layer can add input lag, particularly on flight sims at high polling rates. Disable the overlay; keep the driver.

title: Discord overlay running
label: Discord (with overlay)
reason: Discord's in-game overlay hooks DirectInput and is a recurring cause of joystick stutter and dropped inputs. Discord itself is safe — only the overlay needs turning off.

title: OBS Studio / Streamlabs running
label: OBS Studio / Streamlabs
reason: Game-capture sources hook the rendering pipeline and can add a frame or two of input lag. Acceptable when streaming — but if you left OBS running by accident, close it.

title: Xbox Game Bar running
label: Xbox Game Bar
reason: Game Bar hooks every running game window and captures gamepad input by default. Press Windows key + G to confirm it's open, then disable: Settings -> Gaming -> Game Bar -> Off.
